info.title: Transcode
info.description: Transcode is the video and podcast conversion side of Navigatorr: workers (machines that encode), durable actions (one file, a batch of files, podcast ad cleaning), encoding recipes, candidates and promotion backups. The API reads what exists and what is happening, and writes: starting, cancelling, resuming and retrying actions, recording decisions, changing a batch goal, pausing and draining workers, changing worker slots, saving, deleting and rolling back recipes, cleaning, restoring and discarding backups, classifying and reviewing podcasts, revoking ad references and closing review-queue entries. A write calls the same function as the MCP tool or maintenance route of the same name and keeps every safeguard of it: expected revisions, digests and versions, confirm flags, dry-runs and idempotency keys are passed through, never bypassed (a request that omits one is refused with 400 or 409 exactly as the tool would, or answers the read-only preview). Start with GET /transcode/v1/workers to see the machines, GET /transcode/v1/actions?status=running to see what is encoding, and GET /transcode/v1/actions/{id} for one conversion. Paths use {id} for an action, batch or review-queue id, {name} for a worker or recipe. Lists are offset-based: send offset and limit, follow next_offset until has_more is false (/history is the exception: the audit log has no offset, it answers count and records). Write bodies are JSON (Content-Type: application/json, at most 1 MiB, unknown fields rejected). Errors are JSON {error, code, hint}; the hint names the endpoint to use instead. Authentication: X-Api-Key (or Authorization: Bearer) with the transcode API key, which needs nothing else for a write; a signed-in web console session may write only with the console's own write checks (header X-Navigatorr-Request: 1 and a same-site Origin). This document is public.

get.description: Every transcode worker (a machine that encodes) as a row, plus a summary at the top. Call this first to see which workers exist, whether each is reachable and ready, why it is not (message, admission_note, scheduler_health), whether it is paused (pause) and which builds hold it. put.description: Make a node available until a time: until (RFC3339, optional), margin_minutes (0 to 1440, default 0: the node takes nothing new that long before until) and media_types (a subset of tv, anime, movie; empty means all, so use it for only episodes or only movies). A conversion starts on the node only if its media type is allowed and, when until is set, its estimated encode time fits before until less the margin; without an estimate it does not start there. Once the plan has chosen the encoder family only that family's history is used; before that, the x265 history is (the copy history for a conversion known to be audio-only). A blank entry in media_types is 400 invalid_request. Revisions only go up per node: deleting a window keeps the counter, so for a node with no window revision must be the counter that GET answers in its 404 no_window body. A conversion already assigned to the node but not yet sent that no longer qualifies after the change goes back to the queue; one already sent is left alone. Past closing the node takes nothing new until the window is changed or deleted; running conversions are never touched. revision (optional) must be the one read from the window; a stale one is 409 stale_window_revision. 404 unknown_worker if the name is not configured.

get.description: Actions (durable workflows) of the transcode kind, newest created first, as light rows: transcode_media (one file), transcode_batch (a series or folder, its files are children), clean_podcast_ads, promote_transcode_candidate and benchmark_transcode. Each row is only id, action_name, status, file (the source path), title (a batch's series), result (a conversion's goal, outcome, message and encoder, or a batch's non-zero counts), waiting (why it waits), error, parent_action_id, created_at and updated_at; long text is clipped. VMAF and search evidence, phase timings and costs, budgets, validations, progress and steps are only in GET /transcode/v1/actions/{id}. Filter by status. Every row of a page is a transcode action. Two ways to page: before (send the next_before of the previous page) or offset (send next_offset); has_more says whether to go on. To see every action exactly once, walk with before: it is not disturbed by actions created during the walk nor by actions that leave the status filter. With offset, a new action shifts the pages by one (a row repeats) and an action that leaves the status filter can make one skipped. A page always fits in one answer: when limit rows would not fit, it returns fewer, with has_more true. An empty first page means there are no such actions now. Read-only.

next_before.description: The id of the last row of this page, for before= on the next request. Absent on an empty page.
